tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the websites in this Relvato account, with whether each is ready to run monitors.

tools.name: add_site
tools.description: Start monitoring a website. Returns the site and its setup: until the owner proves ownership (connect the WordPress plugin, or verify the domain — the only option for non-WordPress sites), trigger_scan can run the public monitors by hand 3 times a day (setup.manualRuns); scheduled runs, alerts, upda

tools.name: verify_site
tools.description: Check whether the site's ownership is proven: probes the WordPress plugin connection and/or looks for the domain-verification DNS TXT record / meta tag, or (method gsc / bing) asks Google Search Console / Bing Webmaster Tools. Returns the updated setup state. Docs: https://www.relvato.com/docs/verif

tools.name: start_monitoring_for_goals
tools.description: The onboarding shortcut: pick what matters and Relvato adds the monitors that cover it on the current plan (plus uptime, SSL, errors, maintenance mode and structure). Goals: flows (checkout and sign-in), security, search, design, compliance (law compliance — accessibility today), speed, domain, cust

tools.name: list_checks
tools.description: The monitors that can be added to a site: key, what it catches, whether the current plan allows it, whether it's recommended for this site, and whether it's already added. Before the site's ownership is proven, runsNow says which can run now (started by hand) and which after proof; for a site added

tools.name: add_checks
tools.description: Add monitors to a site by key (from list_checks). Each key reports added / exists / rejected with the reason (plan, active-monitor limit, needs the WordPress plugin). Once the site's ownership is proven, new monitors get a daily schedule on plans that run daily (Pro and up) and a weekly one on Free,

tools.name: dismiss_recommendation
tools.description: Stop recommending a monitor for a site (list_checks marks recommendations), or bring every dismissed recommendation back with restoreAll.

tools.name: calibrate_site
tools.description: WordPress / WooCommerce: have Relvato read the store again (a product to buy, checkout type, guest checkout, currency) after the store changed. Runs in the background.

tools.name: verify_vitals_beacon
tools.description: Check that the real-user Web Vitals beacon is on the site (its homepage, or data already arriving). get_site_settings has the snippet to install.

tools.name: site_overview
tools.description: Plain-language health verdict for a site: what needs attention (real issues vs likely false positives), each monitor with its latest run and schedule, setup state, recommended monitors not yet added, and the account's run usage. On WordPress 6.9+ it also lists the site's AI abilities (WordPress Abil

tools.name: get_site_health
tools.description: How a site has been doing: the share of monitors passing now (the Overview's "Monitors passing") and each of the last 30 days, the trend over 28, 90 or 182 days, each monitoring group's briefing (what needs attention, its likely cause and fix), and — on paid plans — uptime from Relvato's own probes

tools.name: get_performance
tools.description: A site's speed: the performance summary, lab Core Web Vitals, real visitors' LCP / INP / CLS (p75, last 7 days against the 28 before, per page type and device), what slows it (the elements, images and scripts behind slow visits) and the top fixes with steps.

tools.name: get_check
tools.description: One monitor in full: on/off, when it runs (schedule, time zone, re-runs on WordPress updates, random extra runs, and whether the plan allows them), its own settings (the visual monitor's pages with their keys, masks, devices, browsers and threshold; the checkout's product, coupon, shipping and field

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: Recent runs, newest first, optionally for one site, one monitor or one status. Each has the monitor (checkId, checkName, and its key in `journey`), status, trigger, timing and its error / warning; get_run has the detail. For older runs pass `before` (the startedAt of the last run you got).

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: One run in detail: status, error and warnings (each with its key for ignore_finding; ignored ones marked; one Relvato never fixes carries noFix — why, and what to do instead), each step, visual comparisons (each with its comparisonId, links to the screenshot, the baseline and the diff that work for

tools.name: get_fix_prompt
tools.description: For a run that failed or found a problem: the same brief Relvato's own AI answers when the user clicks "Suggest a fix" — the site's detected stack, what the monitor verifies, what changed on the site just before, the exact error and findings, whether it was already failing earlier, and for Google /

tools.name: get_updates
tools.description: WordPress sites: the safe auto-update policy and its recent windows (what was updated, rolled back or skipped, and why), plugin versions held back after a rollback, safe updates or deactivations Relvato made and their outcome, and the hardening settings that are on.

tools.name: get_safe_update
tools.description: Follow a safe update or deactivation: applying → verifying → passed, or reverted with the monitors that broke.

tools.name: get_quarantine
tools.description: Quarantine mode (WordPress, paid plans): 48 hours of hourly security runs after a cleanup, with plugin updates paused. Whether it's available, on, until when, every change it saw (expected or not), which monitors it watches, the runs it would use, and past sessions.

tools.name: get_activity_log
tools.description: WordPress sites: who did what — sign-ins and failed sign-ins (with the network, not the full address), accounts and roles, application passwords, plugin / theme / core updates, setting and file edits, PHP errors and failed emails — newest first, within the plan's history (7 to 365 days).

tools.name: get_notifications
tools.description: The dashboard's notifications: failing monitors, a disconnected or outdated WordPress plugin, a silent real-user beacon, domain and ownership problems, safe updates that need a look, paused Slack or webhook alerts, and billing.

tools.name: get_site_settings
tools.description: A site's Settings tab as values: what update_site_settings may change (name, request pacing, spacing between runs, firewall retry delay, flaky-monitor recovery streak, plugin rollback, counting Relvato's own visits in real-user data), what only the dashboard changes (browser identity, proxy, firewal

tools.name: get_alert_settings
tools.description: Who is told about what: how often (instant, daily / weekly digest), the minimum severity, each channel (email, Slack, webhook — whether the plan includes it, whether it's set up, paused, and `on` = alerts actually go out on it), which sites are muted and which monitor types go to which channel (only

tools.name: get_status_pages
tools.description: Public status pages (title, public link, sites, on/off) and monthly client reports per site (on/off, how many recipients, last sent), plus the report branding. Never a report's private link or recipients' addresses. Edited in the dashboard's Agency page.

tools.name: list_heartbeats
tools.description: A site's heartbeats — cron jobs, backups and scheduled tasks that check in by requesting their own URL: each one's state (new = waiting for its first ping, up, down), schedule (period + grace, in seconds), last ping, when the next is due at the latest, whether the plan covers it, recent missed or fa

tools.name: update_check
tools.description: Turn a monitor on or off, or change when it runs: its schedule (up to weekly on Free, daily on Pro, hourly on Business, every 15 minutes on Agency), re-runs when the WordPress site changes (plugin, theme, core or WooCommerce updates; Pro and up) and random extra runs (Business and up). Only the fiel

tools.name: pause_monitor_group
tools.description: Pause one monitoring group on a site for 1 hour, 24 hours or until resumed (maintenance, a redesign, a migration). The group's monitors that are on are switched off and remembered; when the time is up, or with resume_monitor_group, exactly those are switched back on, as far as the plan allows. Pausi

tools.name: resume_monitor_group
tools.description: Resume a paused monitoring group now: the monitors its pause switched off go back on (a monitor the plan no longer allows stays off, with the reason in keptOff). A group that isn't paused is left as it is.

tools.name: update_visual_monitor
tools.description: Edit the visual regression monitor: add pages (a built-in one by key, or a page of your own by its address on the site, e.g. "/pricing"; up to 10 of your own), rename or re-point a page of your own, change any page's masks (CSS selectors painted over before comparing, for clocks, carousels, ads), re

tools.name: update_check_settings
tools.description: Change a monitor's own settings. Each monitor takes only its sections (get_check lists them as editable.sections): checkout (checkout monitors), devices (flow and page monitors), errorScan, brokenLinks, accessibilityPages (accessibility), uptime (the URL, text that must / must not appear, accepted s

tools.name: add_custom_check
tools.description: Describe in plain words what to verify on a page (e.g. "the Pro plan shows a price", "search for 'shoes' returns results") and Relvato's AI writes a monitor for it, in a minute or two. Follow it with get_check: status goes authoring → proposed (show the user its rationale and steps, then approve_cus

tools.name: edit_custom_check
tools.description: Give a custom monitor a new goal, page, name or mode. Its current recipe is dropped and the AI writes a new one, which needs approving again before the monitor runs.

tools.name: reauthor_custom_check
tools.description: Have the AI write a custom monitor's recipe again: answer its question (status needs-input) with `answer`, or retry after it failed or went stale. The monitor stops running until the new recipe is approved.

tools.name: approve_custom_check
tools.description: Approve a custom monitor's proposed recipe (status proposed) so it runs and alerts from now on. Show the user its rationale and steps first (get_check). A recipe in interactive mode clicks or types on the live site: approve it only after the user agrees, with ack: true.

tools.name: update_site_settings
tools.description: Change a site's operational settings. Only the fields you pass change. Browser identity, the proxy, the firewall token, GitHub and search-engine connections, and deleting the site stay in the dashboard.

tools.name: update_alert_settings
tools.description: Change how often alerts are sent (instant and/or a daily or weekly digest), when the digest goes out, the minimum severity, and whether every run is emailed. Only the fields you pass change. Who gets alerts (the address, Slack, webhooks), muting sites or monitor types, and turning email alerts off s

tools.name: add_heartbeat
tools.description: Create a heartbeat for a job the user runs (cron job, backup script, scheduled task, CI job). Returns its ping URL: the job requests it when it succeeds (e.g. `your-job && curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 <pingUrl>`), and `<pingUrl>/fail` to report a failure (a POST body is kept with the ping). No ping wit

tools.name: update_heartbeat
tools.description: Rename a heartbeat, change its period or grace, or pause / resume it. Only the fields you pass change. Paused: pings are still recorded but nothing is judged or alerted (an open outage ends without a "back" alert); resumed, it waits for its next ping. Deleting a heartbeat stays in the dashboard.

tools.name: trigger_scan
tools.description: Run a site's enabled monitors now — or one group of them (group), or one monitor with checkId, even if it's turned off. Each run counts toward the monthly run quota. Runs go one at a time and take from seconds to a few minutes each, so all of a site's monitors usually take several minutes: the resul

tools.name: cancel_queued_runs
tools.description: Stop a site's runs that are queued but haven't started (after a big trigger_scan, or before maintenance). Cancelled runs can't be brought back: start them again with trigger_scan. The run that's already going finishes; nothing already recorded is deleted. Get the user's go-ahead first.

tools.name: request_ai_fix
tools.description: Ask Relvato's AI to suggest a fix for a run that failed or found a problem (the dashboard's "Suggest a fix"). It answers in a minute or two: read it as aiFix on get_run. Plan-gated. get_fix_prompt gives the same brief for you to reason with yourself, without waiting.

tools.name: apply_fix
tools.description: WordPress sites: apply the one-click fix a run proposes (get_run proposedFix: e.g. clear a stuck maintenance file, turn indexing back on, roll back the plugin update that broke it) through the Relvato plugin, then re-run the monitor to confirm. Only that exact fix can be applied. Tell the user what

tools.name: start_safe_update
tools.description: WordPress sites: for a vulnerable or outdated plugin a run found (get_run warnings with a plugin), update it (or deactivate it) through the Relvato plugin, re-run the monitors that were passing, and undo it if any of them breaks. Counts as runs. Follow it with get_safe_update. Get the user's go-ahea

tools.name: start_quarantine
tools.description: After a hack or a cleanup (WordPress, paid plans): run the security monitors every hour for 48 hours, pause plugin updates (with Relvato plugin 1.77.0+ that pause is a tick box in WordPress → Relvato), and alert on every unexpected change. Uses runs (get_quarantine says how many). Stopping it early

tools.name: extend_quarantine
tools.description: Keep quarantine mode on for another 48 hours from now.

tools.name: send_test_alert
tools.description: Send a test alert on one channel (email, slack or webhook) to check it arrives. Slack and webhooks are on paid plans and must be set up in the dashboard.

tools.name: resume_webhook
tools.description: Turn webhook alerts back on after Relvato paused them for repeated failed deliveries (fix the endpoint first; send_test_alert checks it).

tools.name: report_false_positive
tools.description: Tell Relvato's team a run's result is wrong (it failed or warned about something that's fine). Sends the run's details and your note to Relvato's support team; it changes nothing on the run. To stop being told about a finding, use ignore_finding.

tools.name: ignore_finding
tools.description: Stop a finding (a warning on a run, by its key from get_run) from counting on this monitor: it stays on the run, marked ignored, but no longer alerts or fails later runs. Undo with unignore_finding. Only do this when the user says the finding is expected.

tools.name: unignore_finding
tools.description: Make an ignored finding count again (get_check lists a monitor's ignored findings with their keys; get_run marks them on a run).

tools.name: bring_back_run
tools.description: Relvato AI triage (a site on level "aside") set this failed run aside as likely noise — get_run shows aiTriage.setAside. Make it count as a failure again: in the bell, the digest and site health. No alert is re-sent. Use it when the user says the failure is real.

tools.name: accept_visual_change
tools.description: The visual monitor found a page that changed on purpose (a redesign, new content): make this run's screenshot the new baseline for that page, device and browser. Undo with undo_visual_review. Only when the user confirms the change is intended.

tools.name: ignore_visual_change
tools.description: Ignore the area that changed on this comparison from now on (a clock, a rotating banner): it's added to the baseline's ignored regions. Undo with undo_visual_review. A mask (update_visual_monitor) is often the better fix.

tools.name: flag_visual_change_as_problem
tools.description: The AI review let a visual change pass, but it's actually broken: mark it a failure. The run counts as failed in Relvato and shows as needing attention (notifications, Monitors passing); no message is sent.

tools.name: undo_visual_review
tools.description: Undo the last accept or ignore on this page, device and browser: the earlier baseline comes back.

tools.name: accept_structure_change
tools.description: The structure monitor found a page whose layout changed on purpose: adopt this run's structure as the new baseline for that page (pageKey), or for every changed page on the run (all: true). Undo with undo_structure_review.

tools.name: ignore_structure_change
tools.description: Ignore specific element changes on a page from now on (signatures from get_run metrics.pages[].added / removed / countChanges[].sig), e.g. a widget that comes and goes. Undo with undo_structure_review.

tools.name: undo_structure_review
tools.description: Undo the last accept or ignore on a page of the structure monitor.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_activity_log, get_notifications, get_alert_settings, list_heartbeats, update_check, update_check_settings, send_test_alert · Private data: verify_site, get_activity_log, get_site_settings, get_alert_settings, get_status_pages, update_site_settings, apply_fix · Public sink: get_site_health, get_notifications, get_alert_settings, list_heartbeats, update_check_settings, update_alert_settings, add_heartbeat, send_test_alert, resume_webhook · Destructive: list_sites, add_site, start_monitoring_for_goals, list_checks, add_checks, site_overview, get_check, list_runs, get_run, get_fix_prompt, update_visual_monitor, update_alert_settings, trigger_scan, cancel_queued_runs, request_ai_fix, apply_fix, start_safe_update, start_quarantine, report_false_positive, ignore_finding, unignore_finding, bring_back_run, accept_visual_change, flag_visual_change_as_problem, accept_structure_change.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_activity_log, get_notifications, get_alert_settings, list_heartbeats, update_check, update_check_settings, send_test_alert · Private data: verify_site, get_activity_log, get_site_settings, get_alert_settings, get_status_pages, update_site_settings, apply_fix · Public sink: get_site_health, get_notifications, get_alert_settings, list_heartbeats, update_check_settings, update_alert_settings, add_heartbeat, send_test_alert, resume_webhook · Destructive: list_sites, add_site, start_monitoring_for_goals, list_checks, add_checks, site_overview, get_check, list_runs, get_run, get_fix_prompt, update_visual_monitor, update_alert_settings, trigger_scan, cancel_queued_runs, request_ai_fix, apply_fix, start_safe_update, start_quarantine, report_false_positive, ignore_finding, unignore_finding, bring_back_run, accept_visual_change, flag_visual_change_as_problem, accept_structure_change

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
